prompt:
Aspect ratio 16:9, landscape, 1920x1080. Desktop WEBSITE DESIGN MOCKUP — the FIRST VIEWPORT of a homepage. A screen design, not a photograph, not a poster. No browser chrome, no address bar — page content only, edge to edge.
GROUND: dark warm-black photo-album card page #14120F, fibrous heavy black album stock. Never cream, parchment or sepia.
HEADER REGION, top 58%: one wide panoramic photograph of a narrow Atlantic peninsula city — sea both sides, long sandy beach curving away, pale ochre apartment blocks, palm trees, deep blue Atlantic. Spans ~62% of frame width, positioned right of centre, held by four small white paper photo corners, rotated ~1.5 degrees. One strip of pale ochre washi tape #C98A3E across its top edge. At its upper right, overlapping it, a perforated postage stamp with visible scalloped die-cut edge, tilted ~6 degrees, containing a small photo of a white street sign reading "Cadiz", with a circular postmark ring in muted vermillion #C6362C reading "CADIZ · 03.09.2026".
TITLE BLOCK, upper left on the black card: "Cadiz 2026" handwritten in silver pencil, smaller line beneath "zwei Wochen am Atlantik", then five short lines of small clean sans-serif body text in warm off-white — an introductory paragraph, quiet and readable.
LOWER REGION, bottom 42%, beginning below the photograph: the start of a chronological day sequence, three horizontal entries stacked as rows. Each row: a small square photograph in white paper corners at the left, then a handwritten date in silver pencil ("03.09", "04.09", "05.09"), a two-line summary in off-white sans-serif, and at the far right a small torn-edge paper tab #F2F0EB. The first row's tab carries a deep-blue #0F3B57 notch at its edge; the other two do not. The third row is cut off by the bottom of the frame, showing the page continues.
FLOATING CONTROL, fixed at the lower right corner, no larger than 70x70 px, clearly a small badge and not a panel: a tiny folded paper map seen from above, closed and folded so only its creased outer panel shows, hand-drawn like an old pen-and-ink chart — a simple coastline outline in muted vermillion #C6362C on off-white paper, a thin route line, nothing else. ABSOLUTELY NOT a modern digital map: no map tiles, no street grid, no location pins, no Google Maps or Mapbox styling, no green parks, no blue highways. A piece of folded paper taped to the corner with two small strips of ochre washi tape, slightly raised with a soft honest shadow.
COMMITMENT: the dominant move is the panoramic photograph in white corners on black album card. The day rows below hold still and quiet; the tiny folded paper map in the corner is the only other object that asks to be touched.
PALETTE: #14120F, #0F3B57, #C98A3E, #C6362C, #F2F0EB.
AVOID: serif display typography, centred hero text over full-bleed photo, rounded-corner card grids, gradient overlays, glassmorphism, neon, browser chrome, modern digital map tiles, map pins, drop shadows beyond what a physical object casts.
structural_question: Synthese nach Nutzerentscheid (Henning 20.09.): Option 3 gewaehlt, aber mit dem Panorama als Kopfbereich darueber; Karte wird zum jederzeit verfuegbaren Popout. Erste Fassung zeigte ein Kartensymbol im Stil digitaler Kartendienste — genau das, was der Nutzer vermeiden wollte; neu erzeugt als gefaltete Papierkarte.
